transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-15
Time: 13:00 - 13:56 ET
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Park (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Head of Data, Scoutline), Marco Ruiz (Infra Lead), Evelyn Brooks (CTO, observer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Objective: scope POC decision sprint to select hosting mode for Scoutline's internal assistant product.
- Agreed to run a 48h benchmark on Redwood hosted sandbox; customer to supply sample payloads.
- Key eval axes: latency (p95/p99), cost per 1M tokens, cold-start behavior, data residency & encryption, operational workflows.

Topics: success criteria, traffic profile, benchmark metrics, security docs, timeline.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alyssa: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, um, short agenda — align success criteria, confirm data and traffic profile, decide which hosting lanes to bench. if you're doing camera, feel free, otherwise we'll dive in.
[00:14] Priya: yep thanks, alyssa, quick note, we're trying to decide fast — Q3 launch is target so we need a recommendation within two weeks ideally.
[00:28] Daniel: cool, that timeline helps, we'll scope a 48 hour run and give measurable numbers you can take to your procurement.
[00:45] Marco: just to set context — we run a mix of user queries and backend batch reranks. peak QPS is smallish, maybe 12 rps, but we have bursts up to ~120 for short periods during batch jobs.
[01:02] Alyssa: good, that burst profile is exactly why we usually compare hosted vs dedicated. hosted can absorb short bursts, dedicated gives steady tail latency predictability.
[01:18] Priya: what about private? we're in regulated finance, so data residency and audit logs matter — we may need VPC or on-prem for particular endpoints.
[01:32] Daniel: yeah, private is typically VPC- or on-prem-based; it gives you full control of KMS, HSM, and network isolation but increases ops time.
[01:47] Evelyn: quick question — SOC2 in place? and can you support our SAML SSO for service accounts?
[01:56] Alyssa: yes, Redwood has SOC2 attestation, and we support SAML/SSO and RBAC in the Private/Dedicated lanes; we'll share the paperwork.
[02:12] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[02:30] Daniel: ok, let's define success criteria — from experience I'd recommend three concrete gates: 1) latency SLOs (p95 below 250ms for 1k token prompts), 2) cost per 1M tokens below your threshold, and 3) security/compliance sign-off. does that align?
[02:48] Priya: yes, add quality — model output quality must be within X% of baseline; we'll provide an eval set.
[03:03] Marco: and operational acceptance — we need automated deploys, canary rollouts, and traceability in logs.
[03:18] Daniel: great, we'll include tracing examples and demonstrate rollout flows in the POC.
[03:30] Alyssa: about the eval set — priya, you'll give us redacted transcripts and intent labels?
[03:40] Priya: yes, ~10k rows, redacted, and we'll also provide a traffic histogram.
[03:47] Daniel: perfect. for the benchmark itself, we'll run three model variants: a larger unquantized open model, a quantized 8-bit variant, and a smaller faster model.
[04:02] Priya: do you run prefix cache stuff? we have very conversational sessions so KV cache could help.
[04:10] Daniel: yep, the runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; small note: on some quantized paths very long contexts can change perf characteristics — we'll capture that.
[04:25] Marco: network and egress — if we do private VPC, what are the ingress rules? we want no public endpoints.
[04:35] Alyssa: Private installs can be air-gapped or VPC-peered. we'll send a network checklist. dedicated has controlled egress too but still managed by Redwood.
[04:50] Priya: cost question: Hosted is pay-as-you-go, Dedicated is committed. Rough breakouts?
[04:59] Alyssa: i'll send a preliminary pricing sheet, but high level: Hosted gives lowest friction, variable cost; Dedicated lowers unit cost at commit levels and gives guaranteed capacity. Private has infra & license-like fees.
[05:17] Daniel: and on performance, dedicated nodes let us tune kernel selection and batching aggressivity more aggressively for lower p99 and cost per token.
[05:32] Marco: any specifics about concurrency? our batch reranker needs high concurrency for short windows — will you support burst autoscaling?
[05:41] Daniel: yes, we have autoscaling and burst pools. dedicated can include burst capacity rules in the SLO. hosted has built-in burst too but you have less SLA control.
[05:55] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[06:10] Priya: benchmark metrics — beyond p95/p99, we care about cold-starts and tail latencies, throughput under batch loads, tokenization differences, and determinism.
[06:26] Daniel: we'll capture p50/p95/p99, cold start latencies by model, and end-to-end through your stack. also cost per 1M tokens and cost per inference for reranking flows.
[06:41] Alyssa: quick note on security: we'll include KMS integration notes; private offers customer-managed keys and audit logs. for hosted we provide encrypted-at-rest and customer tenant isolation plus detailed audit events.
[06:58] Evelyn: are audit logs immutable? we need retention 7 years for some flows.
[07:06] Daniel: yes, we can export logs to your SIEM and configure retention; private gives you the most direct control.
[07:20] Priya: timeline — you said within two weeks for decision, what does that look like?
[07:28] Alyssa: proposed: we kick off benchmark this week, share results within 48h after start; review next week; procurement loop after that. so decision by 2 weeks is feasible if all artifacts are shared.
[07:44] Marco: ok, what do you need from infra to run the benchmark?
[07:49] Daniel: network access, sample payloads, traffic histogram, and any firewall/NAT details if you want to run private tests. For hosted sandbox, we only need the payloads and traffic profile.
[08:04] Priya: is there any PII handling during benchmark? we will sanitize but want to be sure of data policies.
[08:12] Alyssa: we recommend redacting PII before sending; Redwood will delete benchmark artifacts per our data retention policy but we'll include a handling statement in the security doc.
[08:25] Speaker 3: (brief pause)
[08:40] Daniel: let's sketch the benchmark plan: 1) ingest sample workload, 2) run steady-state at nominal QPS for 12 hours, 3) run burst tests emulating your daily spikes, 4) run reranking batch throughput tests, 5) capture metrics.
[08:56] Priya: will you run both hosted and dedicated comparisons?
[09:01] Daniel: we can run hosted and a simulated dedicated profile for perf — if you want a full dedicated cluster we can spin a short reserved pool for the POC (needs approval).
[09:15] Marco: cost for spinning dedicated for 48h?
[09:19] Alyssa: small fee or credit against future committed capacity — we'll outline options.
[09:28] Priya: about eval quality — we will run prompts against your models and our current baseline. if generation quality drops, that's a hard stop.
[09:39] Daniel: understoood, we'll present a side-by-side output diff and a scoring rubric. expect some small variability by quantization but we'll measure it.
[09:54] Priya: any known gotchas when moving from hosted to private?
[09:59] Daniel: main ones: network topology and HW parity. private on-prem may have different GPU families which affect perf and kernel availability; quantization paths may differ slightly. Also rollout and monitoring are more collaborative.
[10:16] Marco: do you support our key management, e.g., Azure Key Vault?
[10:21] Daniel: yes, we integrate with common KMS providers; private gives you customer-managed keys for model artifacts too.
[10:30] Evelyn: what about maintenance windows and SLAs?
[10:34] Alyssa: Dedicated gets an SLA and maintenance windows arranged with you. Hosted has best-effort availability but high uptime; we can provide historical uptime metrics.
[10:48] Priya: for the 48h run, we want p95 under 300ms or else we won't consider hosted. is that a realistic gate?
[10:57] Daniel: it's tight depending on model size and token length; for 1k token prompts a 300ms p95 is aggressive. for smaller prompts it's fine. we'll show numbers for your payload lengths.
[11:12] Priya: ok include that as a gate but allow model variant flexibility.
[11:20] Alyssa: notes on observability — we'll show per-route token cost, tracing, and error classification in the console during review.
[11:31] Marco: instrumentations — do you supply opentelemetry spans?
[11:35] Daniel: yes, we export OTEL spans and can forward to your backends.
[11:42] Speaker 1: (keyboard noise)
[12:00] Alyssa: action recap: we'll share pricing and security docs; Daniel kicks off benchmark pending payloads; Scoutline to send samples and network details.
[12:12] Priya: agreed. any blockers for sample redaction?
[12:16] Marco: we have an internal PII scrub tool, should be ready by end of day Friday.
[12:25] Alyssa: cool.
[12:40] Daniel: one more technical detail — for reranking, batching windows matter. small batch sizes can actually improve latency at the cost of throughput; we'll tune it.
[12:55] Priya: and quantization — if we see quality regression above our threshold, will you recommend different quant flags or fallbacks?
[13:03] Daniel: yes, we'll propose quantization profiles or fallback to a larger model for critical flows.
[13:15] Evelyn: procurement angle — what's the purchase model if we pick dedicated? monthly committed capacity?
[13:22] Alyssa: yes monthly reserved capacity with scaling bursts; we can do a short-term pilot contract.
[13:33] Speaker 2: (laughter)
[13:50] Priya: ok, let's talk timeline concretely — can you start the hosted benchmark tomorrow if we send samples today?
[13:58] Daniel: yes we can start within 24 hours of receiving payloads.
[14:06] Marco: i'll send the histogram and redaction plan by EOD tomorrow.
[14:12] Alyssa: great. i'll follow up with an email summarizing owners and dates.
[14:20] Daniel: during the benchmark we'll capture p50/p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens, CPU/GPU utilization, and API error rates. we'll also do a short private-run if you want to test VPC peering.
[14:36] Priya: yes plan for both hosted baseline and a VPC-peered test later in the week.
[14:44] Alyssa: any final questions?
[14:47] Evelyn: nothing more from me.
[14:50] Priya: none. thanks.
[14:53] Alyssa: thanks everyone, we'll send the docs and pricing. meeting adjourned.

--- End transcript ---

Notes on transcription artifacts: occasional mis-heard tokens (e.g., K-V cash for KV cache), filler words preserved, and speaker labels may include generic 'Speaker 1/2' in brief segments.
